# Changing the installer script

This page is for developers who change what a site package does when it is installed: which extensions it switches
on, which settings and siteaccesses it writes, which roles it creates and which repairs run after the content is in
place. It explains how the kernel calls the package's PHP files and how the 7x installer class is built, so you can
change a fork without breaking the chain.

7x and the Exponential Foundation strongly encourage you to share the finished package by pull request to
se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth: see [Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md).

1. [How the files are loaded](#how-the-files-are-loaded)

## How the files are loaded

`package.xml` lists the installer files in `<settings>`:

```xml
<settings>
  <settings-file filename='ini-site.php'/>
  <settings-file filename='sevenx-multi-site-installer.php'/>
  <settings-file filename='install-scripts.php'/>
  ...
</settings>
```

During `CreateSites`, `kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_create_sites.php` reads the site package's `settings-files` and runs
`include_once( <package path>/settings/<file> )` for each file that exists. Nothing else in a file runs by itself:
the kernel then calls the hook functions below when they are defined (`function_exists()`). The same happens whichever
front end started the install: the setup wizard, the kickstarter or `exp:install`
([Install scripts in a site package](../basics/install-scripts-in-a-site-package.md)).

## The hook functions

In the order `ezstep_create_sites.php` reaches them:

| Function | Defined in the 7x package by | What its return value does |
|---|---|---|
| `eZSitePreInstall( $siteType )` | `install-scripts.php` | nothing; runs before the required packages are installed (7x: the installer's `preInstall()`) |
| `eZSiteINISettings( $parameters )` | `ini-site.php` | extra settings for the public siteaccess |
| `eZSiteAdminINISettings( $parameters )` | `ini-admin.php` | extra settings for the admin siteaccess |
| `eZSiteCommonINISettings( $parameters )` | `ini-common.php` | settings for every siteaccess |
| `eZSiteRoles( $parameters )` | `roles.php` | extra roles and policies |
| `eZSitePreferences( $parameters )` | `preferences.php` | user preferences to set |
| `eZSitePostInstall( &$parameters )` | `install-scripts.php` | nothing; runs after content, settings and roles (7x: the installer's `postInstall()`) |
| `eZSiteFinalText( $parameters )` | not used by 7x | text added to the wizard's Finished page |

Each 7x hook file is a few lines that create the installer and return one of its methods:

```php
function eZSiteINISettings( $parameters )
{
    $installer = new sevenxMultiSiteInstaller( $parameters );

    return $installer->siteINISettings();
}
```

> **Warning**
> The hook names are global functions. Only one site package is installed per run, but every file you list is
> included: two files that define the same function end the install with a fatal error.

## The installer class

`settings/sevenx-multi-site-installer.php` defines `class sevenxMultiSiteInstaller extends eZSiteInstaller`
(`kernel/classes/ezsiteinstaller.php`). Its parts:

| Part | Role |
|---|---|
| `initSettings( $parameters )` | collects the values the steps use, with `addSetting( name, value )`; read back with `setting( name )` |
| `addSetting( 'extension_list', array( ... ) )` | the extensions the site switches on, in order (an extension listed earlier wins in settings) |
| `initSteps()` | fills `$this->Steps['post_install']` with the post-install steps |
| `preInstall()` | work before the packages are installed |
| `siteINISettings()`, `adminINISettings()`, `commonINISettings()` | the settings arrays the hooks return |
| `siteRoles()`, `sitePreferences()` | the roles and preferences |
| `solutionName()`, `solutionExtensionName()`, `solutionVersion()` | the names and version the installer records (`simple`, `sevenx_multisite_default_installer`, `1.0` in the 7x class) |

The class file also loads `post-install-fix.php` with `require_once` (repairs shared by the installer); a fork keeps
that line pointing at its own copy.

## Post-install steps

`initSteps()` describes the post-install as a list; `eZSiteInstaller::postInstall()` runs it with `executeSteps()`:

```php
$postInstallSteps = array(
    array( '_function' => 'dbBegin', '_params' => array() ),
    array( '_function' => 'setVersion', '_params' => array() ),
    array( '_function' => 'postInstallFixContentObjectNameLanguages', '_params' => array() ),
    // ...
);
$this->Steps['post_install'] = $postInstallSteps;
```

Each `_function` is a method of the installer (yours or one `eZSiteInstaller` provides) called with `_params`. When a
step reports an error and the error handler answers `ERR_ABORT`, the rest of the list is skipped and the step is kept
in `eZSiteInstaller::abortedStep()` (number, function, count), so the setup knows the post-install did not finish.
The 7x list runs its repairs early for that reason: a comment in `initSteps()` notes that "executeSteps aborts the
chain on the first step that reports an error, and several later steps are fragile".

> **Tip**
> Add a new step as a method named `postInstall<What>( $params = false )`, make it idempotent (safe to run twice),
> and let it log and continue on data it does not find rather than abort, as the 7x steps do.

## Extensions and their tables

Some data a site needs is not content and is not in any package. The 7x installer creates the tables of the
extensions it activates and seeds some of them from the extensions' own files: `declaredExtensionSchemas()` names
`sevenx_themes_media` (schema and data: the layouts, tags and ratings of the demo content), `explayouts` (schema and
data), and the schemas of `ezstarrating`, `ezgmaplocation`, `eztags`, `enhancedselection2`, `cjw_newsletter` and
`syndication`; `extensionSchemas()` adds every other listed extension that ships `share/db_schema.dba` or
`sql/<engine>/schema.sql`. The details are on [Layouts data and share .dba files](../sevenx-multisite/layouts-data-and-share-dba.md).

For your fork this means: a layout or tag you want in a new installation goes into the `share/db_data.dba` of the
extension that owns it, not into the site package.

## Making a change

1. Change the method or add a step in your renamed installer class.
2. Check the syntax: `php -l packages/<name>/settings/<your-installer>.php`.
3. Rebuild the archive ([Rebuilding with build.sh](rebuilding-with-build-sh.md)).
4. Install it in a sandbox and read `var/log/setup.log` ([Testing in a sandbox](testing-in-a-sandbox.md)).
5. Write the change in the package's `<changelog>` and the repository's changelog.

The 7x repository shows the commit style for such changes, for example "Updated: The sevenx_multisite package's
installer activates ezownerchange" (15 October 2026).
